events.title: Tesla Motors incorporated in Delaware
events.summary: Tesla Motors, Inc. was incorporated in Delaware on July 1, 2003. The original Certificate of Incorporation was filed with the Delaware Secretary of State that day (S-1 Exhibit 3.1). A 2024 Texas certificate of formation later restated that Tesla, Inc., formerly Tesla Motors, Inc., was originally incorporated on July 1, 2003.

events.title: Elon Musk becomes Tesla chairman
events.summary: On April 23, 2004, Tesla finalized Series A paperwork; Elon Musk led the round and became chairman of the board. Tesla’s later proxies state he has served as Chairman since April 2004 and as CEO since October 2008. From that appointment he contributed via recruiting, engineering and design work, and capital raising.

events.title: First Tesla Roadster delivered
events.summary: On February 1, 2008, Tesla delivered the first production Roadster (often called P1) to then-chairman Elon Musk, marking the company’s first customer vehicle handoff after earlier timing slips from mid-2007. Tesla later celebrated the anniversary on that date; the production run concluded in early 2012 with roughly 2,450 Roadsters delivered. Next-gen Roadster remains announced-pending — see next-gen-roadster-design-development-pending.

events.title: Tesla Motors IPO closes; TSLA lists on Nasdaq
events.summary: Tesla’s S-1 was declared effective June 28, 2010. The final prospectus priced 13,300,000 shares at $17.00, of which Tesla sold 11,880,600 shares (selling stockholders offered 1,419,400), listed on Nasdaq as TSLA. Tesla’s Q2 2010 press release and later 10-Q state the IPO priced June 28, 2010 and closed July 2, 2010; Tesla received $188.8 million net of underwriting discounts and commissions. Concurrent with the close, Toyota bought 2,941,176 shares for $50.0 million in a private placement. This ledger dates the event to Tesla’s stated close.

events.title: NHTSA classifies Model S wall-adapter fix as a recall (14V-006)
events.summary: On January 14, 2014, NHTSA classified Tesla's fix for NEMA 14-50 wall adapters on up to 29,222 2013 Model S cars as a safety recall (14V-006), citing overheating and fire risk. Tesla had announced the fix on January 10: an over-the-air update (software 5.8.4 or later) that cuts charging current by 25% when it detects unstable input power, plus replacement adapters with a thermal fuse. Musk said the word "recall" should not apply because owners did not need to bring cars in.

events.title: Gigafactory battery plant plan announced
events.summary: On February 26, 2014, Tesla published its plan for the Gigafactory, a battery factory in the southwestern United States targeting 35 GWh a year of cell production and 50 GWh a year of pack output by 2020, enough for about 500,000 vehicles a year. Tesla projected that it and its partners would invest $4-5 billion through 2020, about $2 billion of it from Tesla, and that the plant would employ about 6,500 people. Tesla furnished the announcement in a Form 8-K the same day; groundbreaking near Reno, Nevada followed in June 2014.

events.title: NHTSA closes Model S battery-fire probe (PE13-037) after underbody shield retrofit
events.summary: On March 28, 2014, NHTSA said it had closed Preliminary Evaluation PE13-037 into 15,805 2012-2013 Model S vehicles, opened after two 2013 fires in which road debris pierced the battery pack. The same day Tesla announced a triple underbody shield (a hollow aluminum bar, a titanium plate and an aluminum extrusion) fitted to cars built from March 6 and retrofitted free to existing cars. events.title: First U.S. trial over a fatal Autopilot crash opens in Riverside
events.summary: On September 28, 2023, opening statements began in Riverside County Superior Court, California, in the first U.S. trial alleging that Autopilot caused a death. events.title: California DMV rules Tesla's 'Autopilot' and 'FSD Capability' marketing misleading
events.summary: On December 16, 2025, the California DMV adopted an administrative law judge's finding that Tesla's use of 'Autopilot' and 'Full Self-Driving Capability' in its marketing was misleading and violated state law. The DMV reduced the proposed penalty: it permanently stayed the 30-day suspension of Tesla's manufacturer license and gave Tesla 60 days to stop using 'Autopilot', or face a 30-day suspension of its dealer license. On February 17, 2026, the DMV said Tesla had stopped using 'Autopilot' in its California marketing and would avoid suspension.

events.title: NHTSA opens DP26010 on Robotaxi school-zone speeding petition
events.summary: On October 9, 2026, NHTSA’s Office of Defects Investigation opened Defect Petition DP26010 after receiving a September 23 petition asking it to investigate model-year 2026 Tesla Robotaxis (Model Y and Cybercab) with the Automated Driving System engaged. The petitioner alleges the ADS exceeds posted speed limits in active school zones and supplied three video links. ODI estimates about 1,000 affected vehicles and records four incidents (one ODI complaint and three social-media reports in the petition), with no crashes, injuries, or fatalities. Opening the petition means ODI will decide whether to grant or deny a formal investigation—it is not itself a recall or Preliminary Evaluation. The petition is filed under ODI number 11766676. events.title: Next-generation Roadster unveiled at SpaceX McGregor; reservations open
events.summary: On the evening of October 15, 2026, Tesla unveiled the next-generation Roadster in a livestreamed event at SpaceX's test site in McGregor, Texas. The demo car hung upside down on a ramp using a fan suction system and flew, flipped and landed on cold-gas thrusters. Tesla opened reservations for three versions: Performance (road ready, $50,000 reservation payment), Thrust (rear thrusters, 0-60 mph in under one second, $250,000 reservation payment) and an invite-only, single-seat Rocket version not approved for public roads; $5,000 is due at booking and the balance within 10 days. events.title: Ninth Circuit throws out FSD false-advertising class certification
events.summary: On October 16, 2026, a Ninth Circuit panel (Judges Gould, Bybee and Bress) vacated the orders that let California buyers sue Tesla as classes over claims that cars sold since October 2016 had the hardware for full self-driving. The ruling does not decide the merits, and the underlying false-advertising case before U.S. District Judge Rita Lin remains pending.

events.title: 2026 proxy filed; Annual Meeting set for December 3
events.summary: On October 19, 2026, Tesla filed its definitive proxy statement for the 2026 Annual Meeting, set for December 3, 2026 at 3:00 p.m. Central Time at Gigafactory Texas and online, for holders of record on October 13. events.title: Starship Flight 15: first upper-stage tower catch; booster lost offshore
events.summary: Starship Flight 15 lifted off from Starbase Pad 2 at 4:47 p.m. CT on November 13, 2026, reached orbit and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites. events.title: Tesla opens public Cybercab rides in Dallas
events.summary: On November 19, 2026, @robotaxi posted "Howdy Dallas. Cybercab has arrived in your city," opening public Cybercab rides in Dallas through the Tesla Robotaxi app. Dallas is the second city after Austin to get the two-seat Cybercab with no steering wheel or pedals. Tesla's Robotaxi service in Dallas has run Model Y vehicles unsupervised since April 18, 2026. This delivers the November Dallas launch stated on the October 21 earnings call.

events.title: Supercharger Waitlist goes live at 300 US sites
events.summary: On November 19, 2026 Tesla Charging said its Supercharger Waitlist was live at 300 US Supercharger sites. Drivers join a virtual queue in the Tesla app or on the car's touchscreen, and non-Tesla EV drivers can join through the app. The feature grew from a five-site pilot in California and New York that began in May 2026.

sources.publisher: Tesla Charging (@TeslaCharging) on X, November 19, 2026
TeslaNorth, Tesla Supercharger Waitlist Goes Live at 300 U.S. Sites, November 19, 2026

events.title: Italy approves Tesla Assisted Driving
events.summary: On November 20, 2026 Italy's Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport granted provisional type approval to Tesla Assisted Driving, the supervised FSD renamed for Europe, after a technical feasibility check. Transport Minister Matteo Salvini announced it on X, and Tesla Europe posted "Now approved in Italy, rollout begins soon" without a date. Italy is the 12th EU country to allow the system and the first of the bloc's large markets; an EU-wide vote is not expected before December.

events.statusNote: Approval granted; customer rollout not yet started as of 2026-11-20 (Tesla: 'rollout begins soon').

events.title: UK High Court enters judgment for X against two Creator Revenue Sharing defendants
events.summary: The High Court in London entered judgment against two defendants that X sued in September 2026, alleging a network of accounts manipulated engagement to draw Creator Revenue Sharing payouts. X general counsel James Burnham announced it on November 24, 2026 with the first page of the order. X alleged the network collected more than £207,000; the terms of the judgment are not public.

sources.publisher: James Burnham (@BurnhamDC), X general counsel, on X, November 24, 2026
TeslaNorth, X Says UK Court Entered Judgment in Creator Payout Case, November 24, 2026

events.statusNote: Date is the order date (November 20) as read by TeslaNorth from the posted first page, which also bears a November 23 court stamp; announced November 24. Award amount and terms not shown.

events.title: Tesla begins rolling out FSD v15
events.summary: On November 21, 2026 at 11:24 AM PT, @Tesla posted that FSD v15 was starting to roll out, upgrading every part of the end-to-end driving network. Tesla cited 25x better handling of safety-critical cases, a new Tesla Reality View that visualizes what FSD is planning, and navigation at the start and end of a drive, with later v15 releases to expand that to the entire route. @aelluswamy said it was releasing to the first wave of customers that day. The same afternoon, @TeslaSI posted release notes that include an upgraded vision encoder shared between FSD, Robotaxi, and Optimus. On November 20, Elon Musk said FSD V15 goes to wide release next month.

events.title: SpaceX forgoes BEAD subsidies under new NTIA model agreement
events.summary: On November 23, 2026, NTIA announced a BEAD model agreement for low-Earth-orbit providers that keep their awarded locations but decline the subsidy, and SpaceX agreed to serve its Starlink locations under it. SpaceX must still deliver 100/20 Mbps, pass BEAD performance testing, give new subscribers equipment at no cost, offer a low-cost plan and report every six months. States can sign the model agreement or rebid the locations.

sources.publisher: NTIA BroadbandUSA, BEAD Model Agreement to Accelerate Broadband Deployment, November 23, 2026

events.statusNote: The forgone amount is reported, not stated by NTIA's page: about $738 million (Teslarati, Quartz) versus about $636 million (Telecompetitor, citing administration officials). State adoption is pending; Broadband Breakfast reported that some states were caught by surprise.
